narrative:
The model estimates you have a 23% chance of failing your final year, which is high enough that the school requires you to take remedial courses as a precaution.

The prediction is driven mainly by three key aspects of your situation. The most influential factor is that you do not want to pursue higher education. Among students who passed, every single one expressed a desire to continue studying; your lack of that goal strongly pulls the prediction toward failure. The second most important factor is your reason for choosing this school—reputation—which actually works in your favor and pushes the outcome toward passing. Finally, having no previous class failures also helps your case and nudges the prediction away from failing.

Even though two of these factors speak positively for you, the absence of ambition for further studies outweighs them in the model’s eyes. Because the overall risk remains above the acceptable threshold, remedial courses are mandatory.

To improve, you should seriously reflect on your long-term goals. Talking with a counselor about why higher education feels unimportant right now could help you either rediscover motivation or find a clearer alternative path. Small, consistent study habits and using the extra support sessions will also raise your chances of passing.
